title: Guest-driven System/370 archaeology
summary: Procedure for resolving an unknown guest boundary without coding in the dark.
procedure: Capture exact IA, instruction bytes, ICOUNT, PSW, relevant registers, effective addresses and storage before changing behavior.
Record evidence maturity explicitly: documented architecture, executable-reference corroboration, exact guest proof, permanent replay proof, and sealed checkpoint are distinct states.
Resolve the opcode/exception rule against System/370 documentation and an independent executable reference where practical.
Take a journal point; attach object-scope live behavior; deliberately dirty state when useful; abort and verify exact machine rewind while the live hypothesis survives.
Retry the identical historical state and require architecturally plausible forward progress.
Promote only the proven behavior, prove live-candidate to permanent equivalence, run the accumulated suite, then seal before the next unknown boundary.
After sealing, add the exact artifact SHA-256 and next untouched frontier to project-evidence records; do not retroactively describe unsealed work as sealed.
invariants: Freeze evidence and journal-pointed state remain separate mechanisms.
Unknown opcode symptoms may be caused by an earlier sequencing defect.
No disappearance of a guest diagnostic is sufficient acceptance evidence.
Object-bearing ooRexx helper arguments use use arg; parse arg is reserved for scalar/text parsing where object identity is not required.
